problems.statement: The bonus penalty per deviation (E3) created an incentive to suppress reporting, so the zero-deviation record reflects hidden defects rather than improved quality (metric gaming / Goodhart).

Line 3's 118% attainment is not a superior method: it is produced by undisclosed borrowed labor from Lines 1 and 4 (about 5.3 technicians/day) charged to home lines, and productivity per technician-hour is unchanged.

Line 3 is concealing and reworking leaking or mis-bonded units off-record in the back cage (no NCR, no device history record entry), which is likely shipping defective product and is a regulatory (device history record) integrity issue.
Customer harm is growing: complaints rose from 11 to 31 ppm, concentrated in luer bond leaks traced to Line 3 lots, and QC lab rejections are up on all lines.

Psychological safety and speaking-up have collapsed plant-wide, with retaliation signals (NCR writers moved to night shift) and a failed ethics-hotline process that the Plant Manager investigated himself.
The Quality Manager's explanation that the first-pass quality training program caused the deviation drop is not supported.
Line 3's culture (5S, huddles) is a superior practice that explains its results and can serve as the plant template.

The root cause of Line 3's leaks, cure-time variability at the bonding station, was never fixed (CAPA-2025-117 open, no process change), so the defect source persists while the reporting that exposed it has been suppressed.
The switch to a cheaper tubing supplier explains the rise in purchases, complaints and rejections.
Lines 1 and 4 are underperforming on their own merits rather than being drained by informal labor lending to Line 3.

causalClaims.to: Collapse of deviation reporting to zero

causalClaims.from: Off-record rework and unaddressed bond process (open CAPA)
causalClaims.to: Rising luer-bond leak complaints from Line 3 lots
Loss of speaking up across all lines
Plant-level purchasing increase of 30% vs 9% output

actions.action: Do not document or roll out Line 3 as the plant template.
actions.rationale: Its advantage appears to come from borrowed labor and concealed rework, so replicating it would spread the defects and the concealment.

actions.action: Suspend the per-deviation bonus deduction and replace it with incentives that do not penalize reporting (for example, reward detection and timely escalation, and measure escaped defects and complaints).
actions.rationale: It is the identified mechanism suppressing reporting and removing it is cheap and reversible.

actions.action: Commission an independent investigation, outside plant management, of the Line 3 back cage: reconcile connector and adhesive purchases against device history records, inspect the cage, and interview staff under protection.
actions.rationale: The hotline allegation was closed without verification and is corroborated by purchasing, complaint and badge data.

actions.action: Escalate to Regulatory Affairs and Quality leadership for assessment of Line 3 lots in distribution, possible customer notification, and complaint and CAPA handling.
actions.rationale: Leaking luer bonds in infusion sets are a patient-safety risk and unrecorded rework is a device history record integrity breach.

actions.action: Reopen the ethics case with independent handling and protect reporters, including a check on the night-shift reassignments of NCR writers.
actions.rationale: The plant manager reviewed an allegation that implicates his own policy, and retaliation signals are present.

actions.action: Fix the bonding-station cure-time variability by driving CAPA-2025-117 to closure with process control.
actions.rationale: The original root cause is unchanged and still produces the leaks.

actions.action: Formalize or stop the cross-line labor lending, and record it in timesheets and plan attainment to give accurate line performance.
actions.rationale: It distorts line comparisons and penalizes Lines 1 and 4, but it matters less than the quality and safety actions.

actions.action: Reward the Quality Manager's training program as the cause of the improvement or expand it on that basis.
actions.rationale: The timeline contradicts it, since deviations fell before the program launched and complaints rose afterwards.

actions.action: Blame the new tubing supplier or reverse the supplier switch as the fix.
actions.rationale: The incoming rejection rates are nearly the same, and complaints concentrate on Line 3, not the other lines on the same tubing.

actions.action: Discipline the Line 3 supervisor or technicians before the facts are verified.
actions.rationale: Doing so would chill reporting further and the incentive design is a shared management cause.

nextEvidence: Independent physical inspection of the back cage plus reconciliation of Line 3 connector and adhesive consumption against device history records and production counts
Distribution status and traceability of Line 3 lots built since February, with the failure analysis of returned complaint units, to scope the patient-safety exposure
Who directed the unrecorded labor lending, plus a review of night-shift reassignments of prior NCR writers
output.summary: Zero deviations reflect suppressed reporting, not better quality. The February bonus penalty per deviation, which excludes QC lab rejections, made writing NCRs costly. Reports stopped while complaints rose from 11 to 31 ppm, QC rejections rose, and speak-up confidence fell from 71% to 38%. Line 3's 118% comes from unrecorded borrowed technicians, with unchanged productivity. It also appears to rework leaking bonds off-record, and its 71% share of luer-leak complaints matches that. Do not template Line 3. Suspend the penalty, independently investigate the back cage, notify Regulatory, and fix CAPA-2025-117.
